amendments.rule: A verbless clause supplies its English copula from the construction, not from nothing. In *that it was good*, the supplied *it was* belongs to the unit headed on `טוֹב`; do not mark it `added`. **This covers the copula and nothing more.** Where the ASV instead supplies a whole *lexical* verb for a clause whose Hebrew has none — the allotment formula `וְלִבְנֵי קְהָת הַנּוֹתָרִים ... עָרִים עָשֶׂר` → *And unto the rest of the sons of Kohath* ***were given*** *by lot ... ten cities* — no morpheme's rendering that verb completes, and it is `added` under rule 30, together with any object the ASV supplies alongside it, as in *were given them*. Test by asking which morpheme is there to carry the English: `הָיָה` carries the *have* of rule 43 and the frame of rule 21, a Hebrew verb carries the light verb of rule 44, and a preposition that is itself the predicate carries the copula of rule 49 — but a preposition the ASV has already spent a word on, as in *unto the rest*, carries nothing further, and a clause with no verb in it at all licenses no verb.
amendments.why: Five verses (61, 63, 71, 77, 78) supply *were given*, and 78 supplies *were given them*, for allotment clauses whose Hebrew has no verb; the chapter marks all of them `added`. Rule 20 as written ends with 'do not mark it `added`' and, read beside rules 33, 43, 44, 46 and 49, invites the opposite generalisation — that any English a verbless clause supplies must belong to some morpheme. The line the chapter drew is between a copula, which the construction itself supplies, and a lexical verb, which nothing in the projection licenses. Rule 49 does not reach these clauses, because the `לְ` heading each is already rendered *Unto*, so there is no bare prepositional predicate for a copula to join; and the eight verbless clauses in this chapter that do write a copula (17, 18, 19, 31, 33, 50, 54, 60) all fold it onto their predicate, so both branches are attested side by side here. Amended rather than returned as a new rule so the over-broad closing clause is corrected where a verse pass will read it.

amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amendments.why: vv. 19, 33, 54 and 56 render the *nomen rectum* arthrously — *the families of the Kohathites*, *the fields of the city* — so the ASV writes two *the*s where rule 29's fronting clause assumes one. The clause excludes the case by its own wording ('and renders the rectum anarthrously'), and the sentence that follows it then forbids the only defensible reading, since 'supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present' would leave the chapter's second written *the* with nowhere to go on a two-level chain. The anarthrous branch is attested eight times in the same chapter (48, 49 three times, 57, 67), and the no-*the* branch once (65), so all three sit side by side and the difference is the ASV's rather than the analyst's. The added sentence decides it the way rules 42 and 47 already decide waws and coordinated articles — read which word the English word stands before — and changes nothing about the anarthrous case the rule already governs. Amended rather than added as a new rule so the over-broad sentence is corrected in place instead of acquiring a cross-reference.

conventions: The city-and-suburbs formula וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁיהָ → *with its suburbs*, in vv. 57–81: the waw takes *with* under rule 14, since the ASV does render the connective, just not as *and*; the אֵת is `unrepresented` under rule 16; and מִגְרָשׁ and its suffix are separate units, *suburbs* and *its*. Do not mark the waw `unrepresented` and *with* `added`. The same waw is rendered *also* where the ASV writes it postpositively after the preceding name (57, 67), under rule 51. מִגְרָשׁ has no unit anywhere in the corpus, so *suburbs* here is the precedent a later chapter will read.

תַּחַת in vv. 24 and 37 is tagged R (preposition) by MACULA but is the personal name Tahath in this genealogy, and is aligned to the ASV's *Tahath* — in v. 37 as a nomen rectum taking *of* under rule 19. Rule 38's bar on letting secondary evidence override direct analysis cuts both ways: the morphology tag is wrong about this token, and the surrounding בֶּן ... בֶּן chain is what shows it.

report: Checked all 58 candidate lemma groups and read the verse dump end to end for `added` units, which the lemma-keyed table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways: every difference the table shows is licensed by the ASV's wording or by MACULA's morphology. No patches.

Article placement in construct chains is the chapter's one systematic judgment, and it is consistent. Anarthrous rectum with one written *the* puts it on the article and leaves the construct bare — עָרֵי הַמִּקְלָט → *the cities of refuge* (57, 67), מִזְבַּח הָעוֹלָה and עֶבֶד הָאֱלֹהִים (49), בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים inside the three-level chain of 48. Arthrous rectum with two written *the*s puts one on each — מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי (19), בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי (33), מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי (54), שְׂדֵה הָעִיר (56). No written *the* leaves the article `unrepresented` — הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה → *these cities* (65). The middle branch falls outside rule 29's text as it stands, so it is returned as an amendment.

The city-and-suburbs formula וְאֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁיהָ → *with its suburbs* is identical in all twenty verses that carry it (57–81): the waw takes *with* under rule 14, the אֵת is `unrepresented` under rule 16, and noun and suffix are separate units. מִגְרָשׁ has no corpus precedent at all, so this chapter sets it; recorded as a convention.

The three הַנּוֹתָרִים phrases agree: in 61, 70 and 77 the article takes a plain *the* (rule 15, not rule 41's supplied pronoun) and the participle takes *rest*. The *of* after *rest* goes to the following Hebrew noun where there is one — בְּנֵי in 61, מִשְׁפַּחַת in 70 — and joins the `added` unit in 77, where the words after *rest* are the ASV's own supply *the Levites* and no morpheme is left to carry it.

Supplied English divides cleanly. Copulas are folded onto their predicate in all eight verbless clauses that write one (17, 18, 19, 31, 33, 50, 54, 60); the supplied lexical *were given* is `added` in all five verses that have it (61, 63, 71, 77, 78), with *them* joining it in 78. That line is the chapter's second systematic judgment and is returned as an amendment to rule 20.

One copula sits on something other than a predicate noun: v. 31's *are they whom* joins the relative אֲשֶׁר, because there the relative clause is the predicate and rule 46's first rider gives אֲשֶׁר the supplied antecedent. v. 33's parallel *are they that* splits the other way only because an article morpheme is present and rule 41 assigns it *they that*. Different source, not a split.

BSB: all eight disagreements are documented convention differences and none is an error. Three אֵת (59, 60 twice) and the two articles of הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה (65) are rules 16 and 29 against BSB's practice of attaching a function morpheme to its phrase; לָ in 54 is rule 40's recasting, the ASV writing only *theirs*; the waws of 55 and 66 have no English *and* anywhere in the prepared ASV target. No accepted edge was changed, and the 98.9% figure was not a consideration.

Two conventions recorded, two amendments returned (rules 20 and 29), no new rules, no requests. The validation report's 73 repeated notes are the log gap the conventions close for the two judgments that are not already contract text; the rest of those notes restate rules 14, 16, 18, 19 and 29 and need no entry.
